claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm inquiring about my son Alex. He's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you're inquiring about your son Alex, who is 18 years old.

Since Alex is 18, I need to ask you:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

(For example, this could include things like school, college, university, or an approved apprenticeship or vocational training scheme)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and hasn't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex is 18 and not in approved education or training, I need to check one more thing:

**Is Alex currently in paid work for 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask one more important question:

**Is Alex currently receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have what I need to make a determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided:

- Alex is 18 years old
- He is not in approved education or training
- He is not in paid work for 24 hours or more per week
- He is not receiving benefits in his own right

According to the Child Benefit rules, you would normally qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training. However, since Alex is 18 and is no longer in any form of approved education or training, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

The eligibility for children aged 16 or over is limited to those who remain in approved education or training. Once a young person leaves education or training and is not engaged in any qualifying activity, Child Benefit payments cease.

Is there anything else I can help clarify about this decision?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
I understand. That's disappointing, but thank you for explaining it clearly. No, I don't have any other questions.

<invoke name="exit_loop">
<parameter name="reason">The eligibility agent has provided a clear eligibility determination - that I am not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex because he is 18 and not in approved education or training. The conversation has reached its natural conclusion.</parameter>
</invoke>
